title: Risk Assessment: Tune claude.md files and prompts
summary: Technical risk assessment for unifying prompt criteria into shared markdown files, conditionally assembling CLAUDE.md, and cleaning up dead code. Overall risk is MEDIUM — the approach is sound but has specific pitfalls around container build contexts, GHA trusted-checkout security model, and test coupling that require careful handling.

risks.title: Orchestrator container lacks access to shared/prompts/ at build time
risks.impact: Orchestrator criteria functions would fail with FileNotFoundError at runtime if they try to read shared/prompts/ files
risks.description: The orchestrator Dockerfile (orchestrator/Dockerfile lines 14-22) copies only specific Python packages from shared/ (egg_logging, egg_config, egg_contracts, egg_container). It does NOT copy arbitrary subdirectories. If criteria are placed in shared/prompts/*.md, the orchestrator container will not have these files. The orchestrator runs in its own container (docker-compose.yml line 90-93), not inside the sandbox, and has no volume mount for the egg source repo at the shared/prompts/ path.

mitigation.strategy: Add COPY directive to orchestrator Dockerfile: 'COPY shared/prompts/ ./prompts/' and have the Python functions read from Path('/app/prompts/') with inline fallback. Alternatively, place criteria files in a location already accessible to both systems — e.g., alongside the orchestrator code itself.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — straightforward Dockerfile change, but adds a build dependency that future maintainers must keep in sync

risks.title: GHA trusted-checkout security model interaction
risks.impact: If implemented incorrectly, a malicious PR could inject prompt content into review agents that run with bot tokens
risks.description: The GHA reusable workflows (e.g., reusable-review.yml lines 474-491) implement a two-stage checkout security model: (1) checkout main for trusted prompt scripts, (2) checkout PR code for the review target. The prompt builder scripts (build-review-prompt.sh etc.) run from the main checkout. Currently, inline criteria serve as immutable defaults that cannot be tampered with by PR code. If the scripts are changed to read criteria from shared/prompts/*.md using a relative path like 'cat shared/prompts/code-review-criteria.md', the path resolution depends on which checkout is the working directory at execution time. If the working directory is the PR checkout (not main), a malicious PR could provide a tampered criteria file.

mitigation.strategy: Ensure GHA scripts read shared criteria using an absolute path anchored to the trusted main checkout, not the PR checkout. The reusable workflows already set up the trusted checkout path — scripts should use $GITHUB_WORKSPACE or a dedicated variable pointing to the main checkout. Also maintain hardcoded inline fallback criteria in the scripts so that if the shared file is missing (e.g., during rollout before merge to main), the default criteria still apply. The existing .egg/review-rules.md user-override mechanism intentionally reads from the PR checkout — this is by design and should remain separate from the default criteria loading.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — if paths are correctly anchored to the trusted checkout, the security model is preserved

risks.review_reason: Security-sensitive change to the trusted prompt generation pipeline. Must verify that path resolution in GHA workflows correctly isolates trusted vs untrusted code.

risks.title: Test suite breakage from content coupling
risks.impact: Multiple test files will fail when criteria move from inline strings to file reads
risks.description: Tests in tests/action/test_build_review_prompt.py assert specific phrases like 'thorough', 'ALL issues', 'every', 'context' that appear in the inline default criteria. Tests in tests/action/test_build_agent_mode_design_review_prompt.py assert exact phrases like 'guidelines, not absolute rules', 'Orienting vs constraining', 'Practical balance', 'Benefit of the doubt'. When criteria move to shared markdown files, the bash scripts need to read them at test time. If tests mock the filesystem or run without the shared files present, they will fail. The orchestrator tests (orchestrator/tests/test_pipeline_prompts.py) are lower risk because they test function output behavior rather than exact string content.

mitigation.strategy: Update test fixtures to provide shared markdown files in the test environment. For bash script tests, ensure the test working directory contains the shared/prompts/ files or that the scripts are invoked with correct path resolution. For orchestrator tests, add test cases that verify: (a) shared file is loaded when present, (b) inline fallback is used when file is missing. Run the full test suite before and after changes to catch regressions.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — tests need updating but the pattern is straightforward

risks.title: Rollout timing: GHA scripts reference shared files before they exist on main
risks.impact: After merging the PR, GHA workflows on other PRs could fail if script changes land before shared files, or if the GHA cache serves stale main branch content
risks.description: The GHA trusted checkout checks out the main branch to build prompts. If the PR modifies both the bash scripts (to read from shared/prompts/) AND creates the shared files, these all land atomically on main at merge time, which is fine. However, if the implementation is split across multiple PRs, or if GitHub Actions caches the main checkout, there's a window where scripts expect files that don't exist. Additionally, if partial commits within a single PR are cherry-picked, the script changes could land without the shared files.

mitigation.strategy: Ship all changes in a single PR (as the architect recommends). Ensure every script that reads from shared/prompts/ retains inline fallback defaults — the existing pattern where the script checks 'if file exists, cat file, else use heredoc default' should be preserved for the shared criteria files. This makes the transition backward-compatible. The fallback eliminates any rollout timing risk.
mitigation.residual_risk: NEGLIGIBLE — fallback pattern is already established in the codebase

risks.title: Conditional CLAUDE.md assembly could break future agents that expect full content
risks.impact: An agent invoked without EGG_PIPELINE_ID that needs contract or orchestrator CLI reference would not have it in CLAUDE.md
risks.description: The proposed change excludes contract.md (~2.7 KB) and orchestrator.md (~3.2 KB) from CLAUDE.md when EGG_PIPELINE_ID is not set. Currently all agents get all sections. If a new feature or workflow invokes agents that need contract/orchestrator CLI references outside the SDLC pipeline (e.g., an ad-hoc debugging session that needs to inspect contract state), those agents would lack the relevant instructions. The savings (~1,500 tokens per non-SDLC invocation) is modest.

mitigation.strategy: The mitigation is already built into the approach: EGG_PIPELINE_ID is set for all SDLC pipeline invocations. Non-SDLC invocations (ad-hoc sessions, GHA workflows) genuinely don't need contract/orchestrator CLI references. If a future use case requires them outside SDLC, the condition can be broadened. The slash commands (sdlc.md, show-metrics.md) which reference these CLIs are loaded on-demand and are unaffected. Low residual risk.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — easy to reverse if needed

risks.title: Criteria drift between shared markdown and GHA-specific context
risks.impact: Shared criteria files could diverge from GHA-specific conventions over time if maintainers forget the relationship
risks.description: The architect proposes sharing only criteria content, not output format instructions (conventions). This means GHA scripts will compose: shared_criteria + gha_conventions + user_overrides. The orchestrator will compose: shared_criteria + verdict_format. If someone updates the shared criteria to reference GHA-specific concepts (like 'gh pr review' commands), or if the conventions evolve to assume criteria content that has changed, subtle inconsistencies could emerge. This is the same class of problem the refactoring aims to fix, just at a different boundary.

mitigation.strategy: Add a comment header to each shared criteria file noting which systems consume it (GHA scripts + orchestrator) and that it must remain output-format-agnostic. Add a CI check or test that verifies shared criteria files don't contain GHA-specific terms (gh pr, $GITHUB_REPOSITORY, etc.).
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — documentation and review process suffice

risks.title: Removing claude-rules/ symlink could break Dockerfile or CI that references it
risks.impact: Docker build would fail if Dockerfile still references claude-rules/ after symlink removal
risks.description: The architect suggests removing the sandbox/claude-rules/ symlink and updating the Dockerfile COPY to use sandbox/.claude/rules/ directly. The Dockerfile currently uses 'COPY sandbox/claude-rules/*.md /opt/claude-rules/' (line 117). Docker follows symlinks during COPY, so the current setup works. Changing to 'COPY sandbox/.claude/rules/*.md /opt/claude-rules/' would also work, but the .claude directory name might cause issues with .dockerignore or other tooling that filters dotfiles.

mitigation.strategy: Verify that .dockerignore (if present) does not exclude .claude directories. Test the Docker build locally before merging. Alternatively, keep the symlink as-is — it's functionally harmless and the architect noted this is low priority. The symlink removal could be deferred to avoid unnecessary risk.

risks.title: User-override mechanism (.egg/*-rules.md) behavior change in orchestrator
risks.impact: Extending .egg/review-rules.md to orchestrator reviews changes behavior for repos that have custom rules — they'd now apply in both GHA and local reviews, which may not be expected
risks.description: The architect recommends extending the .egg/review-rules.md user-override mechanism to orchestrator reviews (Q1 in open questions). Currently, user overrides only affect GHA workflows. If extended to the orchestrator, repos with custom .egg/review-rules.md would see those custom rules applied in SDLC pipeline reviews too. This is likely desirable but is a behavioral change that could surprise users who set up overrides specifically for GHA reviews.

mitigation.strategy: Document the behavioral change in the PR description. The user-override files (.egg/review-rules.md etc.) are an opt-in mechanism — users who created them presumably want consistent review criteria. The risk of unwanted behavior is low. If needed, a separate .egg/orchestrator-review-rules.md could be supported, but this adds complexity for minimal benefit.
mitigation.residual_risk: LOW — behavioral change is aligned with user intent

risks.review_reason: Behavioral change that affects all repos with custom .egg/*-rules.md files. Confirm this is the desired behavior.

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: Security-critical: prompt builder scripts must read shared criteria from the trusted main checkout, not the untrusted PR checkout. Implementation must be verified to maintain the existing security model.
areas_requiring_human_review.suggested_reviewer: Security-aware engineer familiar with GHA reusable workflow security model

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: Behavioral change affecting repos with custom .egg/*-rules.md files. Confirm this aligns with user expectations.
areas_requiring_human_review.suggested_reviewer: Product owner or engineer familiar with user-facing configurations

areas_requiring_human_review.area: Scope of shared criteria vs GHA-specific context
areas_requiring_human_review.reason: The architect defers slash command unification (Q2) to a follow-up. This boundary decision (what's shared vs system-specific) has long-term maintenance implications. Confirm the boundary is drawn correctly.

rollback_plan.strategy: Revert the entire PR. The fallback pattern (inline defaults in scripts) means reverting is safe — criteria return to inline, conditional CLAUDE.md logic is removed, dead code cleanup is undone. No data migration or state changes are involved.
steps: 1. Revert the PR via GitHub UI (creates revert commit)
2. GHA workflows immediately use inline criteria again (fallback path)
3. Orchestrator container rebuild picks up reverted code automatically
4. Sandbox container rebuild restores full CLAUDE.md assembly
5. No manual intervention needed — all changes are code-only, no state migrations
rollback_plan.data_loss_risk: NONE — this is a prompt generation change, no persistent data is affected
rollback_plan.downtime_risk: NONE — prompt generation changes take effect on next agent invocation, not mid-execution

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Ship all changes in a single PR to avoid rollout timing issues (R4). The architect's workstream ordering (WS1 -> WS2/WS3 parallel -> WS4/WS5 -> WS6) is logical but all should be in one PR.
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Atomic merge ensures shared files and script changes land together. The fallback pattern handles the pre-merge state.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Add shared/prompts/ COPY to orchestrator/Dockerfile (R1). This is the most likely-to-be-overlooked step since the architect's plan mentions EGG_REPO_PATH as the read path, but the orchestrator runs in its own container where the egg source repo isn't mounted.
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Without this, orchestrator criteria functions will fail in production. The orchestrator container needs the files baked in at build time.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: For GHA scripts, use a path relative to the script's own directory ($SCRIPT_DIR/../shared/prompts/) anchored to the trusted checkout, not a bare relative path (R2).
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Prevents prompt injection via malicious PR code. The scripts already use `$(dirname "$0")` for conventions files — use the same pattern for shared criteria.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Maintain inline fallback criteria in both GHA scripts and orchestrator functions (R3, R4). Use the pattern: if shared file exists, read it; else use inline default.
implementation_recommendations.rationale: Backward compatibility during rollout, resilience against missing files, and makes the transition reversible without a full revert.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Defer the claude-rules/ symlink removal (R7) to a follow-up. It's low value and introduces unnecessary risk in an already large changeset.
implementation_recommendations.rationale: The symlink is functionally harmless. Removing it requires Dockerfile and possibly .dockerignore changes that could break the build for a negligible cleanup benefit.

performance_assessment.token_savings: ~1,500 tokens per non-SDLC agent invocation (40% of CLAUDE.md excluded)
performance_assessment.build_time_impact: Negligible — adding COPY for 4 small markdown files
performance_assessment.runtime_impact: Negligible — file reads are cached by OS, criteria are small (<5 KB each)
performance_assessment.note: The token savings are modest but the cognitive noise reduction (irrelevant SDLC instructions removed for non-SDLC agents) is the primary value. The unification benefit (single source of truth for criteria) is the main long-term win.

security_assessment.threat_model: Prompt injection via malicious PR modifying shared criteria files in untrusted checkout
current_controls: GHA two-stage checkout: prompt scripts execute from main branch, not PR branch
Inline fallback criteria: scripts have hardcoded defaults that don't depend on any file
User overrides (.egg/*-rules.md): intentionally read from PR checkout (opt-in customization)
proposed_controls: Script path anchoring: read shared criteria using script-relative paths from trusted checkout
Fallback preservation: inline defaults remain as fallback if shared files are missing
No new trust boundaries: shared criteria are read from the same trust context as existing prompt scripts
security_assessment.residual_risk: LOW if path anchoring is correctly implemented; the security model is preserved

compatibility_assessment.breaking_changes: None — all changes are additive with fallback behavior
compatibility_assessment.backward_compatibility: Full — inline fallbacks ensure old behavior when shared files are missing
compatibility_assessment.forward_compatibility: Good — shared markdown files can be extended without code changes
affected_systems: Docker build for sandbox and orchestrator containers
